Question: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

Options:
opa. Inflammation of the patellar tendon
opb. Noninflammatory degeneration of the joint
opc. Infection of the joint
opd. Deposition of crystals in the joint
ope. Inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac
